questions.question:
Two masses \(A\) and \(B,\) each of mass \(M\) are fixed together by a massless spring. A force acts on the mass \(B\) as shown in the figure. If mass \(A\) starts moving away from mass \(B\) with acceleration \(a,\) then the acceleration of mass \(B\) will be:

1.\( \dfrac{M a-F}{M} \)2.\(\dfrac{M F}{F+M a} \)
3.\(\dfrac{F+M a}{M} \)4.\(\dfrac{F-M a}{M} \)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\( F_{net}=F+F_s \) Step 1: Find the spring force. Mass \(A\)moves away from mass \(B\) with acceleration \(a\). Therefore, the spring is compressed and exerts a force on mass \(A\). Spring force, \(F_s=Ma \) By Newton's third law, the same spring force acts on mass \(B\) in the opposite direction. Step 2: Apply Newton's second law on mass \(B\). For mass \(B\), net force is, \( F_{net}=F+F_s \) Using, \(F_{net}=Ma_B \\ \Rightarrow F+F_s=Ma_B \\ \Rightarrow F+Ma=Ma_B \\ \Rightarrow a_B=\frac{F+Ma}{M} \\ \Rightarrow a_B=\frac{F+Ma}{M} \) Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.
